Le Grand Récit, c'est une émission RTL q: Le Grand Récit is an RTL show built on an irresistibly simple idea: take a great destiny and ask André Dussollier to tell it. Not read it — tell it. The nuance is everything.
Dussollier n'est pas un présentateur rad: Dussollier isn't a radio presenter reading a teleprompter while thinking about lunch. He's an actor who sets up an era, characters, an atmosphere. Who creates suspense. Who lays out the story with diction so precise that every sentence carries weight. It feels as if someone is telling a story just for you.
La journaliste Isabelle Choquet prend en: Journalist Isabelle Choquet then takes over: she hosts a specialist — historian, journalist or direct witness — to move from story to analysis. A double layer that works perfectly: emotions first, keys to understanding after. As if you'd watched a wonderful film, then the director explained all its mechanics right afterwards.
Quand elle jouait une scène dramatique à: When she played a dramatic scene in her acting classes, she made people laugh without meaning to — comedy was in her. And yet in real life, she really wasn't funny. She was only happy on stage. Her drama teacher predicted her fame very early — she only became famous at 40.
Une star de cinéma qui choisit de s'enga: A film star who chose to enlist in the Free French army when everyone told him to stay in the United States. He ended up a tank commander in General Leclerc's division. He kept that moment to himself all his life — and turned down almost every military role after the war.
Pour montrer à quel point le podcast ne: To show how far the podcast goes beyond history or cinema: how some personalities don't adapt to their era — they transform it. Told with the same seriousness as the Second World War.
Ce qui est fascinant dans Le Grand Récit: What's fascinating about Le Grand Récit is that it doesn't tell the glory. It tells the moment just before. The one where everything could still go either way. The tipping point where a destiny becomes a legend — or might never have. That's precisely what makes the format addictive.
Dussollier ne force jamais l'émotion. Il: Dussollier never forces the emotion. He doesn't dramatise for nothing. He lays out the story. Simply. And you cry anyway. This restraint is a form of respect for the listener — and for the people he's telling about. The result: it feels like a confidence rather than a radio show.
Ce qui est remarquable aussi, c'est la d: What's also remarkable is how long these stories live on. Gaëlle, our guest, summed it up perfectly: she would retell the story to her husband in the evening, unconsciously reproducing exactly the podcast's structure — keeping the suspense, dropping the details one by one. Le Grand Récit creates a chain of transmission. It doesn't stop when the episode ends.
